images.title: Where the Earth sits between the Sun and Saturn
images.purpose: Shows the Sun to Saturn distance, 1.4335 × 10¹² m, on a line, with the Earth at 1.496 × 10¹¹ m, about one tenth of the way.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One long horizontal line from the Sun at the left end to Saturn at the right end, with one marker near the left.
images.exact_structure: One long horizontal line in dark outline. At the left end an amber (#E69F00) filled circle labelled Sun; at the right end a grey (#6B7280) filled circle labelled Saturn, with 1.4335 × 10¹² m under the middle of the line. A teal (#0072B2) dot on the line at about 0.104 of its length from the Sun, labelled Earth above it and 1.496 × 10¹¹ m below it. A thin bracket from the Sun to the Earth dot labelled about 1/10. No other ticks. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Compare exponents first: the distance with 10¹¹ is about a tenth of one with 10¹².
images.description: Shows the Sun to Saturn distance, 1.4335 × 10¹² m, on a line, with the Earth at 1.496 × 10¹¹ m, about one tenth of the way.

image_decisions.why: Placing the Earth on the Sun to Saturn line turns a smaller exponent into a visible short distance.
